subject: Biology
description: Covers Lysosomes, Plastids, and Mitochondrial DNA.

questions.stem: Which organelle is famously known as the 'Suicide Bag' of the cell?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs containing powerful digestive enzymes. They act as the cell's waste disposal system, digesting obsolete components, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria. They are called "suicide bags" (or suicidal bags) because if a cell is damaged beyond repair, the lysosomes rupture and release their enzymes into the cell, entirely digesting (destroying) the cell itself in a process called autolysis.
DECOY BUSTING: Mitochondria are the 'Powerhouses' (making ATP). Ribosomes are the 'Protein Factories'. The Golgi apparatus is the 'Packaging Center'.
EXAM INSIGHT: The highly destructive enzymes inside a lysosome are called 'hydrolytic enzymes', and they only work effectively in an acidic environment (pH ~5.0).

questions.stem: Which of the following cellular components is found EXCLUSIVELY in plant cells and NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Plastids are double-membrane organelles found only in plant and algal cells. The most famous plastid is the Chloroplast, which contains chlorophyll and performs photosynthesis. Other plastids include chromoplasts (which give fruits and flowers their colors) and leucoplasts (which store starch/oil). Animal cells do not photosynthesize, so they do not have plastids.
DECOY BUSTING: Both plant and animal cells are eukaryotic, meaning they both have a Nucleus, Mitochondria, and a Cell Membrane (plasma membrane). However, plant cells ALSO have a rigid Cell Wall OUTSIDE the cell membrane, which animal cells lack.
EXAM INSIGHT: Another major difference is the vacuole. Plant cells typically have one massive central vacuole that takes up 50-90% of the cell volume, while animal cells have many small, temporary vacuoles.

questions.stem: The genetic material (DNA) of a eukaryotic cell is housed within the nucleus. However, DNA is also independently found in which other organelle?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: While the vast majority of DNA is in the nucleus, the Mitochondria contain their own small, circular DNA (mtDNA). Because they have their own DNA and ribosomes, mitochondria are semi-autonomous and can replicate themselves independently of the cell. (In plants, Chloroplasts also have their own DNA).
DECOY BUSTING: Ribosomes are made of RNA and protein, not DNA. The ER and Lysosomes do not contain genetic material.
EXAM INSIGHT: According to the 'Endosymbiotic Theory', mitochondria and chloroplasts were once free-living bacteria that were engulfed by a larger cell billions of years ago. A highly tested fact: Mitochondrial DNA is inherited strictly from the MOTHER.
